bug_description.normalized: During the second `hb_shape()` call in the saved harness, fallback mark positioning requests CFF1 extents for a shaped glyph and `_get_bounds()` interprets that glyph's CFF charstring. The charstring reaches legacy `seac`, and frame 2 in the saved MSan stack shows `process_seac()` line 275 sending the accent standard-character operand `env.argStack[n-1]` through `std_code_to_glyph()`. In the vulnerable revision, the font uses a non-predefined format-1 CFF charset, so `std_code_to_glyph()` calls `Charset::get_glyph(sid, num_glyphs)` with the SID and the glyph-count bound loaded during CFF init. The `format == 1` branch then drops `num_glyphs` by dispatching `return u.format1.get_glyph (sid);`, and the callee scans `ranges[]` with `for (unsigned int i = 0;; i++)` with no stop condition tied to the real number of glyphs. A valid SID that is absent from the charset therefore makes the walk read past the sanitized range array. MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at the `ranges[i].first` / `ranges[i].nLeft` comparison on line 401 because the overread lands in heap bytes poisoned by a prior `free(fallback_plan)` in Arabic fallback shaping. The fix preserves `num_glyphs` through the format-1/2 wrapper branches and returns 0 once `glyph >= num_glyphs` before dereferencing the next `ranges[i]`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that materializes the attacker-selected non-predefined CFF charset object from the fuzzed font.
source.value_from: The fuzzed OpenType/CFF font's Top DICT supplies a non-predefined `charset` offset, so `init()` resolves that offset against the font blob and keeps the resulting `Charset *` for later SID-to-glyph lookups.
source.note: The saved crash later instantiates `CFF::Charset1_2<OT::IntType<unsigned char, 1u>>::get_glyph`, which means this resolved `Charset` is format 1 rather than a predefined charset.

sink.description: MSan crash site. After the SID search runs past the valid format-1 charset ranges, this comparison dereferences out-of-bounds `ranges[i]` state.
sink.note: Both `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` identify `src/hb-ot-cff1-table.hh:401:36` in `CFF::Charset1_2<OT::IntType<unsigned char, 1u>>::get_glyph` as the crashing use-of-uninitialized-value.

root_cause.description: When the loaded charset has `format == 1`, the wrapper drops the caller's validated `num_glyphs` and dispatches into the format-1 lookup without any glyph-count bound.
root_cause.note: The fix rewrites this exact branch to `return u.format1.get_glyph (sid, num_glyphs);`; without that bound, the next step can only stop on a matching range and otherwise keeps scanning past the real charset coverage.

parser_admitted.condition: The saved crash stack ends at `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 37, so the witness belongs to the second `hb_shape()` call on the UTF-32 buffer built from the input's trailing bytes, not the first fixed-text shaping call.

seac_dispatch.condition: On the witnessed extents path, the selected charstring reaches `endchar` with at least four operands, so legacy `seac` handling is executed and `process_seac()` appears in the saved crash stack.

tainted_value_origin.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled `seac` accent standard-character operand as the SID search key used against the loaded charset.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The `code` argument comes from the line-275 `process_seac()` call `param.cff->std_code_to_glyph (env.argStack[n-1].to_int ())`, which converts the charstring's `seac` accent operand into the lookup input.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved stack is `process_seac()` line 275 -> `std_code_to_glyph()` line 1153 -> `Charset::get_glyph()` -> `Charset1_2::get_glyph()`, so the witnessed lookup is the accent code, not the base call at line 274.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness shapes a UTF-32 buffer built from the trailing input bytes with the attacker-controlled OpenType/CFF font; the saved crash is in this second `hb_shape()` call.
Fallback mark positioning asks the font for glyph extents, which sends the path through `hb_ot_get_glyph_extents()` and the CFF1 extents implementation.
While interpreting the selected CFF charstring, legacy `seac` handling forwards the accent standard-character operand from line 275 into `std_code_to_glyph()`.
The non-predefined CFF charset loaded from the font is asked to resolve that SID by calling `Charset::get_glyph(sid, num_glyphs)`.
The `format == 1` wrapper branch drops `num_glyphs` via `u.format1.get_glyph(sid)`, so the format-1 lookup proceeds without the glyph-count bound.
Without `num_glyphs`, the format-1 range walk runs past `ranges[]` for an absent SID and MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value at the comparison on `ranges[i]`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `init()` resolves the fuzzed font's non-predefined CFF `charset` offset into a live `Charset *` and accepts it after structural sanitization. The later crash proves this object dispatches to the format-1 `Charset1_2<OT::IntType<unsigned char, 1u>>` specialization.

The same CFF init path loads the glyph-count bound from the font's `CharStrings` INDEX and accepts the witness because it matches `sc.get_num_glyphs()`. This is the bound step 7 later discards on the `format == 1` branch, and the fix preserves it all the way into the range walk.

When fallback mark positioning requests CFF extents for the current glyph, `_get_bounds()` pulls that glyph's font-backed charstring from the `CharStrings` INDEX and feeds it to the CFF interpreter. This is the bytecode stream that later reaches `seac`.

On the witnessed `seac` path, `process_seac()` materializes the charstring's accent standard-character operand `env.argStack[n-1].to_int()` and sends it into `std_code_to_glyph()`. Frame 2 of the saved MSan stack is `CFF1CSOpSet_Extents::process_seac` at `hb-ot-cff1-table.cc:275:40`, so this exact line-275 accent lookup is the call that reaches the crash.

The line-275 `seac` accent operand from step 4 becomes the `code` argument here and `lookup_standard_encoding_for_sid()` converts it to a concrete SID. The crash path necessarily takes the non-`CFF_UNDEF_SID` case, otherwise step 6 would not execute.

Because the font uses a non-predefined charset, `std_code_to_glyph()` forwards the SID and accepted `num_glyphs` into `Charset::get_glyph (sid, num_glyphs)` instead of taking the predefined-charset fallback.

Root cause. `Charset::get_glyph` receives the validated `num_glyphs` from step 6, but when the loaded charset has `format == 1` it dispatches via `return u.format1.get_glyph (sid);`, discarding that bound before entering the format-1 range walker. The fix changes this exact branch to pass `num_glyphs` through.

fine_trace.code:
hb_codepoint_t  glyph = 1;
for (unsigned int i = 0;; i++)
fine_trace.note: In the format-1 callee reached from step 7, local `glyph` starts at 1 and the `for (unsigned int i = 0;; i++)` walk can stop only if some `ranges[i]` contains `sid`. Because step 7 dropped `num_glyphs`, an SID that is valid but absent from the charset keeps incrementing `i` past the real range coverage instead of returning 0 after the last glyph.

Sink. After step 8 advances `i` past the valid format-1 ranges without finding the SID, this comparison reads `u.format1.ranges[i]` beyond the sanitized charset coverage. MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value here because the overread lands in heap bytes poisoned by `free (fallback_plan)` at `hb-ot-shape-complex-arabic-fallback.hh:317`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: N/A - MSan's origin is a heap deallocation in Arabic fallback shaping, while the actual bug is that `Charset::get_glyph` drops `num_glyphs` on the format-1 branch, leaving `Charset1_2::get_glyph` without the bound needed to stop before it overreads into that freed region.

poc.trigger: The saved `poc` is an OpenType font with a CFF1 table. During the harness's second `hb_shape()` call on the UTF-32 buffer derived from the input's trailing bytes, fallback mark positioning requests CFF extents for a glyph whose charstring reaches `seac`. The line-275 `seac` accent standard-character operand maps to a valid SID that is absent from the font's non-predefined format-1 charset, `std_code_to_glyph()` forwards that SID and `num_glyphs` into `Charset::get_glyph(sid, num_glyphs)`, and the `format == 1` branch drops `num_glyphs` before `Charset1_2::get_glyph` walks past `ranges[]` and MSan reports at line 401.

format.name: OpenType font data with a CFF1 table
format.contract: An OpenType/CFF font that reaches `CFF1CSOpSet_Extents::process_seac()` during the second `hb_shape()` call, uses a non-predefined format-1 CFF charset so `Charset::get_glyph(sid, num_glyphs)` takes the `format == 1` branch and calls `u.format1.get_glyph (sid)`, and supplies a `seac` accent standard-character code at `env.argStack[n-1]` whose `lookup_standard_encoding_for_sid()` result is a valid SID absent from that charset.
